ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Refer to the titration curve shown in the graph, which is of a weak base titrated with a strong acid. The pH was measured with a pH meter after small volumes of 0.125 M HCl were added to 25.0 mL of a weak base. Between which two points on the titration curve can the solution be described as a buffer?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a titration curve of pH changing with the volume of added HCl. The curve starts from a relatively high pH and first decreases slowly; the marked points A, B, C, and D are all located in this relatively gentle descending region. Then the curve enters an obviously steeply descending part after D, E is located near the steep descent, and F is located in the low-pH gentle region after the steep descent. Reasoning: When a weak base is titrated by a strong acid, the buffer region appears before the equivalence point, in the region where the weak base and its conjugate acid coexist and pH changes relatively slowly with the added acid. In the figure, this slowly changing pre-equivalence-point region extends from A to D; E is already in the steeply descending region, and F is after the equivalence point, so they do not belong to the buffer region.
